newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - July 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - July 29.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Philippine president Fidel Ramos says he will not be a lame duck president in the last year of his term. (PHILIPPINE DAILY INQUIRER)
- Philippine president Fidel Ramos vows to launch an all-out war aginst lawless elements, particularly drug lords. (PHILIPPINE STAR)
- About 20,000 rallyists march near the House of Representatives to denounce what they say is the failure of the Ramos administration to improve the lives of the poor. (CHRONICLE)
- President Fidel Ramos submits to Congress a national budget proposal of 540.8 billion pesos for 1998. (MANILA TIMES)
- The central bank cuts its key overnight interest rates by three percentage points to 22 percent. (ALL PAPERS)
- Registered foreign direct equity investments reach $235.5 million from January to May this year. (PHILIPPINE STAR)
- The Philippine annual value of produciton index rises 0.5 pecent in May, while the volume of production index falls 0.5 percent, the National Statistics Office says. (MALAYA)
